35. (1) Any party aggrieved by any judgment,
order,  decree,  conviction  or  sentence,  entered
or imposed after inquiry or trial by a Primary
Court may, subject to any law and in accordance
with any law, regulation or rule governing the
procedure and manner for so appealing, prefer
an appeal therefrom to the Court of Appeal for
any error in law or in fact:
Provided that where there is no such law,
regulation or rule governing the procedure and
manner for so appealing, the provisions relating
to appeals from a Magistrate’s Court shall apply
to an appeal in a criminal matter or proceeding
and the provisions relating to appeals from a
District  Court  shall  apply  to  an  appeal  in  a
civil matter or proceeding.
